title: 20 Gastonia, Shelby high school athletes for the 2025-26 sports season - NewsBreak
text:
By Joe L Hughes II ,
20 hours ago
The 2025-26 high school sports season saw its share of memorable games, moments, noteworthy performances, and plenty of state championships.
However, what athletes in Cleveland, Gaston and Lincoln counties made the greatest impact over the course of the previous sports year? After much research, here are 20 tri-county standouts who left their mark.
BASEBALL, SOFTBALL HONORS: See the Gastonia, Shelby baseball, softball all-conference, all-state teams
DOUBLE UP: North Lincoln baseball wins back-to-back NCHSAA titles. Here's how
EPIC PERFORMANCE: Cherryville baseball's Bumgardner hurls no-hitter to start NCHSAA 2A finals
Beck Armstrong, Mountain Island Charter Mountain Island Charter’s senior captain put a bow on a stellar high school career by winning the NCHSAA 1A/2A state title in the 100-yard backstroke event in February. It was the fourth consecutive year in which Armstrong claimed state gold in the event.
Brock Bumgardner, Cherryville Bumgardner hit .430 this spring, with 24 extra-base hits — including six home runs — and 59 RBIs. More than a slugger, the Cherryville junior finished with a 10-3 pitching record, a 2.61 ERA and 92 strikeouts, including a no-hitter in the NCHSAA 2A state championship series.
Drew Dixon, Burns The Bulldogs’ senior standout hit better than .450 this season, along with 10 home runs, 11 doubles, three triples and 41 RBIs. Playing most of the nine positions this season, Dixon was named Southern Piedmont 2A/3A/4A and NCBCA 4A baseball Player of the Year.
Jaxon Dollar, East Lincoln Dollar excelled in football and boys hoops. A Georgia football recruit, he caught 54 passes for 1,190 yards and 20 touchdowns this past season for the Mustangs. He also averaged a double-double with 21 points and 10.3 rebounds, along with 6.3 assists and 3.2 steals on the basketball court.
Lan Farmer, Shelby Farmer finished as Cleveland County’s all-time leading passer with 10,365 yards and 132 touchdown passes. More importantly, the Gardner-Webb signee went out on top, leading the Golden Lions to an NCHSAA 3A state championship. Farmer also helped Shelby boys hoops to a Southern Piedmont 2A/3A/4A tournament title.
Olivia Ferraro, North Lincoln No one earned more NCHSAA state gold this year than Ferraro. The North Lincoln student-athlete claimed individual state gold in cross country, indoor track (1,600-meter run) and outdoor track (1,600-meter run), helping the Knights to team championships in each one.
Josiah Guyton, Lincolnton The 6-foot-4, 165-pound guard scored a team-high 24 points per game while shooting 65% from the field, including 40% from beyond the arc. Voted the Southern Piedmont 2A/3A/4A Player of the Year, he also averaged 8.4 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 3.1 steals per game.
Oshauna Holland, Stuart Cramer A Wake Forest women’s hoops signee, she averaged 33.5 points, 8.4 rebounds, 7.2 steals, 7.1 assists and 1.4 blocks during her senior campaign. She finished as the state’s all-time girls basketball scoring leader in 5-on-5 competition with 3,252 points.
Maddie Huffman, Kings Mountain Huffman enjoyed a strong senior softball campaign, finishing with a 16-3 record with 248 strikeouts, helping the Mountaineers to a Big South 5A/6A title and a berth in the NCHSAA 6A West finals. Huffman finished as one of the best pitchers in Kings Mountain softball history with 787 career strikeouts.
Phillip Johnson, East Gaston Won NCHSAA 4A state gold in the 200-yard individual medley and 100-yard breaststroke. Johnson also helped East Gaston’s 200-yard freestyle relay team place fourth at the NCHSAA 4A state meet.
Jackson Kroh, North Lincoln Was named the Most Outstanding Performer of the NCHSAA 5A swim meet after claiming individual state gold in the 100-yard butterfly and 100-yard backstroke, in addition to winning top honors with a pair of the Knights’ relay teams.
Jaleila Littlejohn, North Gaston Littlejohn averaged a double-double this past season, scoring 31.5 points per game along with 12.8 rebounds, helping the Wildcats earn their first postseason berth since 2018. She set a North Gaston girls hoops single-game record by scoring 50 points against Crest on Jan. 16, 2026.
Johnathan Moore, Ashbrook After helping the Ashbrook football team to an undefeated regular season and a Big South 5A/6A title, Moore claimed the NCHSAA 6A wrestling championship at 285 pounds with a 7-1 decision over Southern Guilford’s Brian Bellerand. The Lenoir-Rhyne football signee capped his senior campaign by placing third in the shot put and discus throw.
Addy Morehead, Bessemer City softball In her freshman season, Morehead tied the Gaston County single-season softball record with 12 home runs. She also batted .500 with nine doubles, two triples and 54 RBIs, while finishing with an 11-8 pitching record, a 2.64 ERA and 154 strikeouts.
Kaylin Pardo, West Lincoln The West Lincoln softball slugger hit .671 this past season with eight home runs and 45 RBIs, helping the Rebels to a Southern Piedmont 2A/3A/4A championship. Pardo started the season with a 23-game hit streak.
Bentley Sly, Stuart Cramer Sly became one of 17 wrestlers to finish as a four-time NCHSAA state champion, claiming the 4A state wrestling title at 150 pounds over Washington’s Tucker Massie. Each of his titles came at different weight classes, joining previous ones earned at 144, 132 and 120 pounds.
Jaleel Smith, Hunter Huss Smith scored 30 points per game along with 7.1 rebounds, 4.9 assists and 4.9 steals, helping the Huskies to the NCHSAA 5A state title. For his work, he was named to the MaxPreps Sophomore All-America Team. Smith also set a program record with 59 points in a January win over Crest.
D’Various Surratt, Crest An enforcer on the back end of the Charger defense, Surratt finished with 34 tackles (one for a loss), four interceptions, two fumble recoveries and eight passes defensed. The NC State football recruit helped Crest to a 13-2 record and an NCHSAA 5A title.
Will Varner, Kings Mountain Varner won his second straight NCHSAA title, winning the Class 6A wrestling title at 165 pounds. After winning state gold at 150 pounds the previous winter, Varner finished his senior campaign with a 27-3 record.
Jyi Watkins, South Point After averaging 10.2 points, three rebounds and 2.9 steals per game on the basketball court, Watkins made her presence felt on the soccer pitch, leading South Point with 32 goals and eight assists during the 2026 campaign. She helped the Red Raiders to a 24-3-1 record and a berth in the NCHSAA 5A West final.
This article originally appeared on The Gaston Gazette: 20 Gastonia, Shelby high school athletes for the 2025-26 sports season
